newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-FIORENTINA FANS STAGE SILENT PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA FANS STAGE SILENT PROTEST.

text.p: Diehard Fiorentina fans, whose team are staging a media blackout, held a silent protest of their own during a European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final second leg against Benfica on Thursday.

The fans in the Fiesole curve section of the stadium remained resolutely silent as the players appeared on the pitch and stayed that way for the entire first half in a protest against the banning of some of their number.
"Silence to defend our rights," declared a large banner draped along the end of the Stadio Comunale.
Some 27 Fiorentina fans have been identified and banned from the Italian club after a recent league match against Juventus, when the visiting team's coach was stoned.
The Italian news agency Ansa quoted the fans saying in a statement that they would repeat the protest in all future league and cup matches at the stadium.

"This initiative has nothing to do with the players' behaviour or the poor performances of the team, but is for ourselves. We cannot accept the way in which the 27 have been identified, banned and condemned without trial," they said.

At half time the fans rolled up the protest banner and brought out their flags. When the teams reappeared, the fans broke into deafening chants and the Fiesole end vanished behind a barrage of red flares and smoke.
Fiorentina players have been refusing to talk to the media in an unrelated protest.
